plan.hypothesis: Travel planning feels like work; seeing scattered travel intentions become one understandable trip should turn overwhelm into anticipation.

creative_rationale.title: The View Is Waiting
creative_rationale.treatment: At a Dubai waterfront café, one traveler is ready to explore; their companion is still negotiating a guidebook and loose planning notes. A raised 'one moment' finger gently interrupts their departure. The planner turns to their phone. An explicit editorial cut takes us into a grounded, readable device close-up showing the real tict overview. We return to the same human take: the guidebook closes, the planner looks up, and the waiting companion gets their smile. The trip finally feels more interesting than the planning.
creative_rationale.construction: Use one continuous generated ten-second human scene, interrupted at its midpoint by a five-second product insert. This preserves cast and location continuity without requiring matching independently generated people. The opening is already a human travel moment, not a title or a collection of photographs. The product answers an established need; the return to the travelers completes the scene rather than abandoning it for a screenshot.

format.typography: Use a verified locally available sans-serif, not an assumed Figma match.
format.safe_area: Keep essential copy and brand artwork within x=60–640 and y=170–1080.

human_direction.location: An outdoor café beside Dubai Creek, with water and creekside architecture behind the travelers. This connects to the supplied UAE, Dubai overview without asserting that this café is an itinerary entry.
human_direction.performance: Affectionate impatience, not an argument. The planner's divided attention is the problem: a guidebook, loose notes, a waiting companion. The release is a closed book and an exchanged look, not a magical interface operation.
human_direction.camera: One seated-eye-level medium two-shot, gentle forward movement, natural afternoon light. Keep the planner's face, hands and companion readable in the vertical composition. The phone screen always faces away from the camera.
human_direction.continuity: Play source seconds 0–5 before the product insert and 5–10 afterward. Both passages come from the same generated take; no matching second cast is requested.

product_direction.presentation: A deliberately separate studio insert: a generic portrait handset resting flat on a broad cream plinth, with a charcoal bezel, restrained contact shadow and diagonal warm light. Build the simple geometry deterministically in Remotion. Composite the exact capture inside the handset; do not place it into generated footage.
product_direction.movement: At 5 seconds, establish the handset with a screen approximately 400 pixels wide, centered below the external brand label. From 5.8–6.4 seconds, enlarge the entire handset and capture together to a screen width of approximately 600 pixels. Let the lower handset leave the frame naturally. Settle with 'UAE, Dubai' and the four planning categories in the central reading area, then hold until 10 seconds. This is a camera-like push, not an app scroll.
product_direction.external_artwork_and_copy: Place the exact logo above the handset, approximately 130 pixels wide. Beside it, outside the interface, set 'Demo interface · data not real' in readable dark sans-serif. Both remain fixed throughout the insert.
product_direction.evidence: The exact overview puts UAE, Dubai together with Stays, Flights, Activities and Car Rentals. That visible grouping supports the organizational hypothesis. No taps, loading states, category expansion, automatic import or creation sequence are demonstrated.
product_direction.data_integrity: Keep the screenshot intact, including its inconsistent demo dates and any prices or controls visible in the wider framing. These are supplied interface pixels, not advertised prices or real bookings. Do not emphasize totals or the RESERVE control, activate them, correct the data or construct a cleaner replacement screen.
product_direction.readability_gate: Check the final settled framing at 720-pixel output width: destination and category names must be readable, with no glare or perspective distortion across them. The brief establishing view is not intended for reading every field.

audio_choice.reason: A modest instrumental pulse gives the waiting gesture a little friction and carries momentum through the product insert. No narration is needed to explain what the actors already show, and the viewer can read the app without competing speech.
audio_choice.execution: Use creek_pulse from time zero at one fixed, low volume. Repeat or trim the procedural sketch to exactly 20 seconds. No gain automation, dialogue, café ambience, paper foley or synchronized sound effects are assumed.
audio_choice.compromise: This is a simple procedural musical sketch, not a bespoke cinematic arrangement. Picture rhythm carries the emotional change. There is no spoken brand name; visible spelling remains tict.

execution_risks_and_compromises: The ten-second generation must deliver a readable waiting gesture, a phone glance around the midpoint and a relaxed look up afterward. This is a performance request, not a guaranteed timed result. Review before assembly; stop if the intended midpoint cut cannot be made coherently.
Hands, paper persistence and phone orientation are generation risks. Keep props few and movement ordinary. Reject melting objects, distracting anatomy or a visible invented screen.

The device insert is an honest editorial cut to a stylized studio setup, not the reverse angle of the generated phone. No screen tracking, rotoscoping, reference conditioning or photorealistic 3D rendering is promised.
The app demonstration remains a static approved capture with a short camera move. It proves an overview exists, not that tict automatically resolved the travelers' notes or booked their trip.
The scene suggests anticipation within Dubai, not a before-and-after transportation claim. No named attraction, accommodation or purchased activity is promised.
Use logo and mascot directly, preserving complete artwork and aspect ratios. Do not regenerate or deform either asset.

Any tool failure, unusable generated action, missing local asset, illegible product framing or unexpected charge stops production with the specific blocker reported. No silent substitution or automatic regeneration.

music.basis: Supplied local procedural music capability; verify before execution.

material_cost_quote.catalog_assets: Already local; no material requests or external cost.
material_cost_quote.control: The quote excludes continuing authoring and judging consumption. Recheck the live balance before execution. No authorization to exceed the shared $20 ceiling, incur unquoted charges or automatically retry generation.

beats.intent: SEE: view_waiting, source 0–5 seconds. Open directly on the companion leaning forward to leave the Dubai waterfront café. The planner raises a gentle 'one moment' finger, glances between an open guidebook and loose notes, then looks down at their phone. Show faces and the inviting water beyond, not a tabletop-only study. No title. HEAR: creek_pulse begins immediately, quiet and even. TRANSITION: cut on the planner's downward eyeline to the separate product insert; do not attempt a moving-screen replacement. CONNECTION: the visible problem is fragmented planning holding up a shared travel moment.

SEE: Exact trip_plan inside the grounded handset composition, with logo and the external demo-data label. Establish for 0.8 seconds; push the complete device closer over 0.6 seconds; hold the readable destination and category rows for 3.6 seconds. Keep all interface pixels unchanged and introduce no interaction. HEAR: uninterrupted creek_pulse at the same volume. TRANSITION: cut back to the existing human take, not another destination shot. EVIDENCE: UAE, Dubai and the four planning categories share one overview. COMPROMISE: this demonstrates organization visually, not a functioning trip-creation flow.

SEE: Resume view_waiting, source 5–10 seconds. The planner lowers the phone, closes the guidebook over the notes and looks up with a small, genuine smile. The companion responds; their attention turns together toward the waterfront. Let the final shared look breathe rather than accelerating into a montage. HEAR: the same fixed-volume music, with no invented café sound. TRANSITION: cut from the relaxed human composition to the mascot's open-armed pose on cream. CONNECTION: relief becomes anticipation through behavior; no completed booking or instant organization is claimed.

SEE: A complete end composition appears at the cut and remains for five seconds. Exact logo centered near y=290 at 280 pixels wide; complete mascot centered beneath it at approximately 520 pixels wide; 'Create your trip.' near y=950 in approximately 52-pixel dark sans-serif. Use #FFFCEE throughout, generous spacing and the mascot's original yellow. No typewriter reveal, fabricated app button, store badge, URL or download claim. HEAR: creek_pulse continues at its fixed level and ends at 20 seconds. SOURCES: logo and mascot only. PURPOSE: an unmistakable, readable invitation to act after the human scene has resolved.

materials.prompt_text: Ten-second cinematic live-action continuous medium two-shot, vertical 9:16. Two adult friends at an outdoor cafe beside Dubai Creek; sunlit water and creekside architecture behind them. Seated eye-level camera, gentle push forward, warm natural light, understated clothes. First half: one friend leans forward ready to leave; the seated planner raises a gentle 'one moment' finger, looks between an open travel guidebook and two loose notes, then checks a phone held with its screen facing away from camera. Second half: the planner lowers the phone, closes the guidebook over the notes and looks up with a small relieved smile. The companion smiles back; both turn their attention toward the waterfront. Affectionate impatience becoming anticipation, not an argument. Few props, natural hands, no dramatic wind. Keep both faces and gestures visible. No cuts, dialogue, readable lettering, visible screen content, logos, captions or graphics.

materials.mood: Warm, lightly propulsive instrumental anticipation. Restrained and spacious rather than triumphant; a simple repeating pulse that supports natural human action and leaves room to read the app. No vocals.

review.review_method: Inspected all 100 sampled frames via 20 timestamped strips, then native-resolution frames around the reported events.

judge_resolution.reason: At 2.1–2.2 seconds the man is picking up/handling the dark object; the claim that nothing handles it is incorrect. This does not clear the separate geometry defect.

At 5.7–5.8 seconds an opening cover reveals objects behind it. A single reveal does not by itself prove teleportation; continuity of the device identity through the longer sequence is the real concern.

confirmed_findings.reason: The handled dark phone-like object becomes a wide bending black cover/page surface against the guidebook. It does not retain the rigid handset identity established at the beginning.
Both people relax and smile before the planned product insert. The planned downward phone eyeline at the midpoint is absent; the book is never cleanly closed.

review.decision: Retain as failed take; do not silently crop away or accept its confirmed geometry defect. Test one explicit prop-choreography revision within experiment 022.

request.prompt_text: One continuous ten-second medium two-shot, vertical 9:16, warm realistic travel commercial. Two adult friends at a waterfront cafe beside Dubai Creek. Open guidebook and two notes lie motionless on the table. The seated man holds one rigid smartphone vertically in his left hand throughout the entire shot, back toward camera, screen never visible. First five seconds: his friend leans forward ready to leave; he raises his right index finger to ask her to wait, looks at the guidebook, then concentrates on his phone. They are not smiling yet. After five seconds: he looks up from the phone and gives her a relieved smile; she smiles back, both look toward the water. His left hand and phone stay still. Right hand rests on the table. No page turning, no book closing, no moving papers, no putting down or rotating the phone. Gentle camera push, natural faces and hands. No cuts, dialogue, titles, readable signs, logos or graphics.

review.assembly_scope: Diagnostic editorial salvage using only the approved excerpt ranges below. The complete source is rejected, not production-approved. Final render requires a separate review.

confirmed_event.evidence: At 5.0 the complete phone lies on the palm; at 5.3 it has a shortened triangular silhouette; by 5.4 the hand is open and empty with no placement or stowing motion. Native frames 0051, 0054, 0055 and 0056 confirm the Gemini finding.

review.editorial_salvage_hypothesis: An explicit five-second product insert can bridge two usable excerpts while excluding the defective object transition entirely. This preserves the cast and location but is not a repair of the generated source.

mandatory_source_edit.implementation: At composition fps=30 use two muted OffthreadVideo instances: opening startFrom=0, endAt=120, playbackRate=0.8 inside a 150-frame Sequence; return startFrom=180, endAt=300, playbackRate=0.8 inside a 150-frame Sequence beginning at frame 300. Check the installed Remotion API semantics. Never play the complete take or include any excluded source frame. Keep the original four output beat boundaries.

review.observed_action: The woman gestures toward her companion's phone while he is occupied with it. A guidebook and money-like loose papers lie on the cafe table. After the excluded transition both smile and look toward the waterfront. No guidebook closure occurs.
plan_deviations: The woman, not the male planner, makes the initial finger gesture.
No guidebook closure or on-camera putting-away action is available. Do not claim or fabricate either action.
Source seconds 4 through 6 are omitted; remaining passages are slowed to 0.8x to keep the approved 20-second output duration.
The waiting-versus-anticipation performance is less explicit than requested and remains a creative review concern.
review.uncertainty: Sampled frame review does not prove absence of all motion artifacts. An editorial time ellipsis is acceptable to test, but the causal link and emotional strength remain unverified.

render_result.local_fix: Removed endAt props; the outer 150-frame sequences bound each 0.8x excerpt. Installed Remotion applies endAt to the internal sequence duration, not the desired slowed source endpoint. The original hint and model output both used this incorrectly.

assessment.summary: The video follows the 20-second four-beat structure using an editorial salvage approach to bridge two live-action passages with a 5-second product insert and a final call-to-action end card. However, the soundtrack includes spoken dialogue referencing Paris, which violates the music-only audio contract and introduces a location contradiction with the Dubai visuals.

observations.description: Opening human two-shot at an outdoor cafe beside Dubai Creek. A man holds a smartphone with its back facing the camera while looking down. A woman seated across gestures toward his phone/hand. An open travel guidebook and paper notes lie on the table. Spoken audio is heard: 'I think we should take the train to go to Paris. That is a great idea.'

Editorial cut to a product insert screen on a cream background (#FFFCEE). The top area shows the 'tict' logo and the text 'Demo interface · data not real'. Below, a smartphone display displays the 'UAE, Dubai' trip overview with category rows (Stays, Flights, Activities, Car Rentals). Between 5800ms and 6400ms, the device composition pushes closer and holds until 10000ms.

Cut back to the live-action scene at the Dubai Creek cafe. Both travelers are smiling and looking toward the waterfront. The smartphone is no longer held in the man's hand. The guidebook remains open on the table without being closed.

Cut to a static end card on a cream background (#FFFCEE) featuring the 'tict' logo centered near the top, the yellow location-pin mascot with outstretched arms in the center, and dark text 'Create your trip.' near the bottom.

issues.description: The audio track contains spoken English dialogue about taking a train to Paris ('I think we should take the train to go to Paris. That is a great idea.'). This violates the audio contract specification (music mode using 'creek_pulse' with no dialogue) and creates a narrative conflict with the Dubai visual setting.
issues.intended_effect_considered: The dialogue was likely included to simulate conversation between the travelers, but it directly violates the contractual audio mode policy and geographical context.

audio_claim_verification.method: Decode final MP4 and original procedural WAV to mono 44100 Hz float PCM; find the codec offset by FFT correlation within +/-4096 samples, fit one scalar gain and compare aligned waveforms, including the alleged first-five-second dialogue window. No ASR or another model call. Raw unaligned correlation was only 0.087; offset correction is necessary for AAC delay.
audio_claim_verification.original_judge_claim: Spoken dialogue about taking the train to Paris during 0–5 seconds.
audio_claim_verification.adjudication: The specific spoken-Paris-dialogue allegation is not supported: correlation exceeds 0.9995 in both windows after a 1882-sample codec offset correction; source video has no audio and the only rendered audio asset is the hash-matching procedural oscillator WAV. Treat this as a confirmed judge false positive, not a creative-quality pass.

first.criterion: Grayscale standard deviation below 1 on downsampled frames; diagnostic for unintended uniform background, not a general aesthetic metric.

final.criterion: Grayscale standard deviation below 1 on downsampled frames; diagnostic for unintended uniform background, not a general aesthetic metric.
